textes.La « dame à la lampe » de la guerre de C: The “Lady with the Lamp” of the Crimean War was first of all a statistician. Her diagrams showed that soldiers died more from disease than from wounds, and they got military hospitals reformed.
textes.Autodidacte de Madras, il écrit en 1913: A self-taught man from Madras, in 1913 he wrote to Hardy, at Cambridge, a letter full of astonishing formulas. Hardy visited him in hospital in taxi number 1729, “a rather dull number.” “On the contrary, it is the smallest number expressible as the sum of two cubes in two different ways.”
textes.Il invente la machine qui porte son nom: He invented the machine that bears his name in 1936, broke Enigma during the war and asked the question of thinking machines in 1950. A long-distance runner, he narrowly missed selection for the 1948 Olympic marathon.
textes.En 628, il écrit les premières règles de: In 628, he wrote the first rules for calculating with zero as a number in its own right: a number minus itself gives zero, and the product of two debts is a fortune. He was wrong on only one point: for him, zero divided by zero was zero.
textes.À la Maison de la sagesse de Bagdad, il: At the House of Wisdom in Baghdad, around 820 he wrote a treatise on solving equations by al-jabr, “restoring.” The word gave us “algebra,” and his Latinized name, Algoritmi, gave us “algorithm.” He solved everything in sentences and figures, without a single symbol.
textes.Fils d'un marchand pisan installé à Béja: The son of a Pisan merchant settled in Béjaïa, in Algeria, he learned the Indian numerals there. His Liber abaci (1202) taught merchants the rule of three, interest and currency exchange. The sequence that bears his name is just an exercise about rabbits in it, and Indian mathematicians knew it before him.
textes.À 19 ans, il construit une machine à cal: At 19, he built a calculating machine for his father, a tax collector. In 1654, with Fermat, he invented probability theory to divide the stakes of an interrupted game. Then he applied it to God: that is the wager, where you bet a finite life against an infinite gain.
textes.On ne sait presque rien de lui, sinon qu: Almost nothing is known about him, except that he taught in Alexandria. His Elements is the most copied textbook in history. To King Ptolemy, who wanted a shortcut: “There is no royal road to geometry.” The retort is only reported seven centuries later.

textes.La philosophie est écrite dans ce très g: Philosophy is written in this grand book, which stands continually open before our eyes, I mean the Universe. […] It is written in the language of mathematics.
textes.Réussir trois quiz de Logique sans faute: Pass three Logic quizzes without a mistake. You are now at the level of a Swiss high school student in 1896.
textes.Einstein n'a jamais été mauvais en maths: Einstein was never bad at math. At his school-leaving exam in Aarau in 1896, he scored 6 out of 6, the top grade, in algebra and geometry. He said he had mastered differential and integral calculus before the age of 15.
textes.Maîtriser l'arithmétique et les fraction: Master arithmetic and fractions. The AI finally finds you equal to yourself.
textes.Le signe « = » est inventé en 1557 par l: The “=” sign was invented in 1557 by the Welshman Robert Recorde, tired of writing “is equal to.” He chose two parallel lines of the same length because, he said, “no two things can be more equal.” It took more than a century to catch on.
textes.Le nombre d'or n'est pas partout: The golden ratio is not everywhere
textes.Maîtriser les proportions et les pourcen: Master proportions and percentages. From now on, you measure before you marvel.
textes.On dit le nombre d'or caché dans le Part: The golden ratio is said to be hidden in the Parthenon, the Mona Lisa or the nautilus shell. The measurements that “prove” it pick their reference points after the fact, and the nautilus spiral does not fit. The mathematician George Markowsky sorted it out in 1992: almost nothing is left.
textes.L'aiguille trop chanceuse: The needle that was too lucky
textes.Maîtriser les probabilités. Le hasard, l: Master probability. Chance doesn't cheat. People do.
textes.En 1777, Buffon montre qu'en lançant des: In 1777, Buffon showed that by dropping needles on a wooden floor, you can estimate π. In 1901, the Italian Lazzarini claimed to have found 3.1415929 in 3,408 throws, accurate to six decimals. Far too good: the number of throws was tailored to land on 355/113.
textes.Maîtriser la logique formelle. Ne relise: Master formal logic. Don't reread your foundations the night before printing.
textes.En 1902, Gottlob Frege imprime le second: In 1902, Gottlob Frege was printing the second volume of his great work, which grounds arithmetic in logic. A letter from Bertrand Russell pointed out a paradox that brought everything down. Frege added in an appendix: nothing is more unwelcome to a scientist than to have the foundations of his building give way just as the work is finished.
textes.Maîtriser l'algèbre et les équations. Vo: Master algebra and equations. You had more time than Galois. And fewer duels.
textes.La légende veut qu'Évariste Galois ait i: Legend has it that Évariste Galois invented his whole theory the night before the duel that killed him, in 1832, at twenty. In fact, he had been working on it for years. That night, he reread, corrected and summarized. In a margin: “I have no time.”
textes.Le test t, outil de base des statistique: The t-test, a basic tool of statistics, was published in 1908 under the pseudonym “Student.” Its author, William Gosset, was a chemist at Guinness in Dublin, and the brewery forbade its employees to publish under their own names. He wanted to choose the best barley from few samples.
textes.Maîtriser la géométrie et la trigonométr: Master geometry and trigonometry. Here, π is not put to a vote.
textes.En 1897, la Chambre des représentants de: In 1897, the Indiana House of Representatives unanimously passed a bill by an amateur physician that in effect set π at 3.2. A mathematics professor who happened to be there, Clarence Waldo, alerted the senators, who postponed the bill indefinitely. It was never passed.
textes.Maîtriser les suites, les limites et l'i: Master sequences, limits and infinity. There are several infinities, and you have just crossed one.
